platformStudy.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing. Create one extraordinary wide 3:2 product campaign photograph for The Bureau of Provisions website. Reference images are product identity references, not compositions to copy. Preserve the bottle's actual cylindrical silhouette, clear hinged domed hood flipped open, oval front latch, folding stainless steel straw to left and broad stainless drinking spout to right, side metal rings and twin character straps, navy BoP heraldic greyhound/leopard crest. Use an ivory version of the reference bottle.
Scene: a perfectly symmetrical, quaint European railway waiting room, sage green panelled wall, rose-pink upholstered bench, a single burgundy suitcase far right, small centred analog clock high on the wall showing 14:17. The bottle is the hero in the foreground, exactly centred on a small square dark burgundy plinth, large and exceptionally sharp, entire bottle visible from x=40% to 60% of image, lid top at y=24%, base y=88%. Straps arranged tidily on either side, no hands. Behind it at the far right, small distant deadpan uniformed station attendant sitting upright with folded newspaper, staring directly ahead. A tiny empty ticket window far left. Quiet situational absurdity: the bottle is ready; the train emphatically isn't. A Wes Anderson cinematic tableau: rigorous frontal symmetry, orthographic feeling, muted pastel sage and dusty rose, oxblood accents, soft warm afternoon light, 35mm film texture, meticulous set dressing, droll stillness. Sophisticated product editorial photograph, tactile materials, real polished stainless mouthpieces, clearly transparent hood. Leave uncluttered sage wall on both sides of bottle for HTML feature callouts. No rendered callout labels, no arrows, no added advertising typography, no watermark. Only product's existing crest branding. Product dominates, attendant is secondary and tiny.

crest.prompt: Edit target: the attached Bureau of Provisions crest. Background extraction only. Remove all the beige paper background everywhere, including enclosed areas inside the shield, between letters, inside the banner, within the leopard and crown, and between fine linework. Preserve every navy ink mark and all original lettering, proportions and arrangement exactly: reading greyhound, tennis leopard, crown, BoP shield, Bureau of Provisions banner and DEPARTMENT OF THIRST. Flat navy ink on fully transparent background, no white fill, no beige fill, no shadow, no surrounding rectangle, no new texture. This is a precise logo background removal, not a redesign. Output a transparent PNG.

strapIntegration.prompt: Edit target: the attached station product photograph. Make ONLY a precise material integration correction to both bottle straps. The reading greyhound on the left strap and tennis leopard on the right currently resemble stuck-on patches/decals. Make both navy animal illustrations look like ink screen-printed DIRECTLY INTO the ivory woven textile straps: no separate rectangular patch, no badge, no sticker, no raised edges, no separate light-colored printed panel. Remove the patch/panel seam around each animal illustration while preserving the strap's structural stitching, leather attachment tabs, metal clips, overall shapes and positions. Have the navy ink subtly follow cloth weave, perspective, folds and existing light/shadow. Preserve the animal designs and navy ink color. Keep EVERYTHING else identical: bottle shape and BoP crest, transparent open hood, steel straw and spout, station attendant and suitcase, clock, bench, sage wall, pink palette, frame composition, light and photograph dimensions. Do not add text or change product mechanisms.
